requirements.requirement: The system must route all evaluation requests through the caching service before invoking score computation logic.
The system must return cached evaluation results when a valid cache entry exists for the given input parameters.
The system must invoke score computation and persist results when no valid cache entry is found.
The system must preserve the existing API response schema and field structure when serving cached results.
The system must ensure that cached and non-cached responses are indistinguishable to the frontend in format and semantics.
The system must support both provider and clinical trial evaluation flows through the cache-integrated facade.
The system must pass all original input parameters unchanged to the caching layer for key generation.
The system must log whether each evaluation request resulted in a cache hit or miss.
The system must fall back to direct computation if the caching service is unavailable.
The system must return a successful evaluation response even if cache read operations fail.
The system must not introduce additional required fields or remove existing fields in the API contract.
The system must ensure deterministic cache usage such that identical inputs always result in the same cache key lookup.
The system must include cache-aware evaluation results in any LLM-generated explanation without altering explanation structure.
The system must ensure the LLM does not reference caching behavior explicitly in user-facing explanations.
The system must provide identical LLM outputs for cached and non-cached evaluation inputs given the same data.
The system must ensure LLM prompts are constructed using evaluation data regardless of whether the data originated from cache or fresh computation.
The system must prevent partial or incomplete cached data from being passed to the LLM for explanation generation.
The system must maintain latency improvement when serving cached results compared to non-cached computation paths.
